stages.reference:
Create a high-quality visual MATERIAL REFERENCE for the worn player armor texture described below. This image will be used as Image B in a later controlled UV-material transfer. It is NOT a UV atlas, not a 64x32 texture, not a texture sheet, not an inventory icon, not a Minecraft item sprite, not a model render, and not a game screenshot.

SUBJECT:
CHESTPLATE / GOLD WORN ARMOR

MATERIAL IDENTITY:
Dense forged gold armor with warm muted yellow-gold metal, compressed hammering, fine scratches and contact wear, soft edge rounding from use, and very restrained tarnish in recesses. Keep the metal rich and heavy without neon yellow, mirror gloss, or decorative luxury styling.

PIECE / USE:
A torso armor study: emphasize broad chest and abdominal coverage, shoulder transitions, attachment points and load-bearing seams. Large surfaces should show believable hammering or material grain without invented ornament; exposed ridges and lower edges carry more wear than protected central planes.

ASSET-SPECIFIC MATERIAL BEHAVIOR:
The large forged-gold surfaces should be slightly more subdued than ceremonial jewelry, with fine directional hammering, shallow scratches from contact and controlled tarnish around joints and underside edges.

ART DIRECTION:
Grounded dark-fantasy realism. Ancient, weathered, somber, tactile and physically believable. Restrained saturation, soft neutral diffuse lighting, controlled micro-detail and honest material response. Show the armor as a practical wearable object/material study with enough visible surface area to understand construction and material behavior. Use a simple unobtrusive neutral studio-like background; no dramatic scene lighting, colored cinematic light, text, UI, diagrams, inventory presentation or decorative props.

REFERENCE FUNCTION:
The visual master is the material and appearance language only. Make color relationships, material response, manufacturing character, aging and wear easy to read. Do not present an atlas or explain UVs. Do not copy a Minecraft render aesthetic, pixel art, voxel style, cartoon/anime treatment, glossy toy finish, generic photoreal product photography, exaggerated fantasy ornamentation, or invented armor geometry. Do not redesign the original armor silhouette or invent major components, engravings, gems, spikes, crests, straps or closures that are not intrinsic to the original identity.


FINAL REFERENCE REQUIREMENT:
Show a restrained, believable close visual study of this exact armor material and piece. Keep the source identity recognizable and the material physically coherent from edge to edge. The result should provide useful appearance information for transferring onto an already-correct player armor UV atlas without contributing new geometry or UV structure.
